title: Word to Phone Number Converter: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Word to Phone Number Converter: Turn a word or phrase into the digits on a telephone keypad — CALL-ME becomes 2255-63. Learn how to use it, the formula behind…
content:
The [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Turn a word or phrase into the digits on a telephone keypad — CALL-ME becomes 2255-63. Enter your word or phrase and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Convert a word or phrase into the digits it spells on a telephone keypad: A, B and C are 2, D, E and F are 3, and so on through W, X, Y and Z on 9. Digits, spaces, dashes and other characters pass through unchanged, so CALL-ME becomes 2255-63 and 1-800-FLOWERS becomes 1-800-3569377. Businesses use this to check vanity numbers — a phone number that spells a word is far easier to remember than a random string of digits.

## How to use the Word to Phone Number Converter

Start by typing or pasting your word or phrase. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type the word or phrase — letters, digits and dashes are all fine.
2. Read the converted number below.
3. Try a vanity number before you buy it, to check it spells what you think it does.

## Formula

Each letter maps to its keypad digit: ABC→2, DEF→3, GHI→4, JKL→5, MNO→6, PQRS→7, TUV→8, WXYZ→9. Digits and punctuation are kept as they are.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. CALL-ME becomes 2255-63: C→2, A→2, L→5, L→5, M→6, E→3. 1-800-FLOWERS becomes 1-800-3569377. Try the same figures in the [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. ## Why vanity numbers work

A number that spells a word is easier to remember because memory works in chunks: FLOWERS is one chunk, 3569377 is seven. Studies of advertising recall consistently find vanity numbers easier to remember and more likely to be dialled than random ones, which is why 1-800-FLOWERS built a whole business on it. The trade-off is that letters only cover 2–9 — a vanity number can never contain 0 or 1 as a letter, so spellings are sometimes creative.

## The keypad layout

The mapping is the standard telephone keypad, settled in the 1960s: 2 holds ABC, 3 holds DEF, 4 holds GHI, 5 holds JKL, 6 holds MNO, 7 holds PQRS, 8 holds TUV and 9 holds WXYZ. The 1 key has no letters, and 0 has none either (it used to carry the operator). Q and Z were added to 7 and 9 in the 1960s — older phones had no Q or Z at all.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Digits and dashes pass through unchanged, so full numbers like 1-800-FLOWERS convert in one go.
- A vanity number cannot spell 0 or 1 — those keys have no letters.
- Check the spelling before you pay for a vanity number: one wrong letter changes the number.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do letters convert to phone numbers?

Each letter maps to the digit on its telephone keypad key: ABC is 2, DEF is 3, GHI is 4, JKL is 5, MNO is 6, PQRS is 7, TUV is 8 and WXYZ is 9. Try it with your own numbers in the [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What number does CALL-ME spell?

2255-63. C is 2, A is 2, L is 5, L is 5, M is 6 and E is 3 — the dash stays where it is. Try it with your own numbers in the [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can a phone number spell the letters Q or Z?

Yes — Q is on the 7 key with P, R and S, and Z is on the 9 key with W, X and Y. Older phones had no Q or Z, but the modern layout includes them. Try it with your own numbers in the [Word to Phone Number Converter](/word-to-phone-number-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
